old_factual_claim_variants: observation arm was prognostically the worst
observation arm was worse at baseline
poorly differentiated 33% against 22% and 19%; node positive 62% against 60% and 54%
replacements.corrected_short_text: Observation had more favorable grade/nodal features but more positive margins. Primary HR 0.86 (95% CI 0.66–1.11; P=.25) remains nonsignificant; adjusted HR 0.75 is hypothesis generating.
replacements.corrected_long_text: In Table 1, observation had poor differentiation 19% versus 33% with fluorouracil/folinic acid and 22% with gemcitabine, and node positivity 54% versus 62% and 60%. Positive margins were more frequent in observation:19% versus 14% and 15%. The mixed baseline differences do not establish a global ranking of the arms. The primary periampullary comparison was nonsignificant (HR 0.86, 95% CI 0.66–1.11; P=.25); the adjusted secondary estimate (HR 0.75, 0.57–0.98; P=.03) is hypothesis generating and does not independently establish ampullary-specific benefit.
caveats_to_preserve: Prespecified adjustment uses the same trial patients
Adjuvant treatment remains an individualized reasonable choice rather than proven subgroup benefit

old_factual_claim_variants: no PFS or OS is reported for this subgroup
No progression-free or overall survival is reported for the pancreatic subgroup
no survival data for pancreatic subgroup
provides no survival data for that subgroup
replacements.corrected_short_text: Prespecified pancreatic cohort: median PFS 9.2 months (95% CI 5.5–11.2); OS not reported. Single-arm estimates do not establish comparative survival benefit.
replacements.corrected_long_text: The prespecified pancreatic efficacy cohort comprised 36 KRAS wild-type patients. The main Results text reports median PFS 9.2 months (95% CI 5.5–11.2), citing supplementary Table S7/Figure S8; pancreatic OS is not reported. Investigator response was 15/36 (42%, 95% CI 25–59) and central response 16/36 (44%, 28–62). The study has no control arm, so these outcomes do not establish comparative benefit.

old_factual_claim_variants: 36 of 158 patients in the primary efficacy population
replacements.corrected_short_text: 204 treated; 161 in the primary-efficacy set; 158 measurable for investigator response assessment; 36 pancreatic efficacy patients (42 pancreatic treated overall).
replacements.corrected_long_text: eNRGy treated 204 patients, including 42 with pancreatic cancer. Its primary-efficacy set contained 161 patients, including 36 pancreatic patients. Three of the 161 lacked measurable disease for the investigator-assessed primary response analysis, leaving 158 for that analysis. Do not label 158 as the entire primary-efficacy population.
caveats_to_preserve: Investigator and central measurable-disease sets are not interchangeable
All 36 pancreatic efficacy patients KRAS wild-type

old_factual_claim_variants: short-follow-up exclusions falling on early progressors
patients excluded for short follow-up are disproportionately early progressors
at least 24 weeks of follow-up before data cutoff
replacements.corrected_short_text: The efficacy cutoff required first dose≥24 weeks before data cutoff. Later initiation accounted for most exclusions; disproportionate exclusion of early progressors is not established.
replacements.corrected_long_text: The primary-efficacy definition required first dose at least 24 weeks before the data cutoff and other specified molecular/treatment criteria. Forty-three of 204 treated patients were outside that set, mainly because they began treatment later. The criterion did not require remaining progression-free or on treatment for 24 weeks, and the report does not establish that exclusions disproportionately removed early progressors.
caveats_to_preserve: Preserve sponsor/open-label assessment limitations without inventing an exclusion mechanism
